title: Redwood December 2026 All-Hands
summary: Leadership update covering end-of-year metrics, product roadmap milestones (Dedicated capacity improvements, Private deployment GA plan), reliability investments, hiring tempo, and company OKRs. Q&A focused on pricing, SOC2 roadmap, and private deployment timelines.
action_items: Priya Singh: Share updated roadmap deck and timelines by 2026-12-12
Tariq Patel: Postmortem on Nov. 28 incident and remediation plan by 2026-12-09
Jules Ramirez: Send hiring priority list for Q1 2027 by 2026-12-10
next_steps: Product to schedule deep-dive demos for Sales and Customer Success
Ops to publish incident report and follow-ups
People to open Q1 hiring reqs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Elena Morales (CEO), Marcus Green (CTO), Priya Singh (Head of Product), Tariq Patel (VP Eng), Jules Ramirez (Head People), Sara Kim (Head Sales), Ben Foster (Head Ops) + all staff (Zoom).

[00:00] Elena (CEO): ok hi everyone thanks for joining our last all hands of the year, I know it s late for some regions so we ll keep it tight, um we have a packed agenda, quick company update then product and engineering deep dive, hiring and then Q&A.
[00:45] Marcus (CTO): quick note on audio, recording is on, we ll push slides after.
[01:10] Priya (Head of Product): first thing, product highlights: Redwood Dedicated improvements shipped in November included dynamic autoscaling and better isolation for multi-tenant workloads, we re seeing a 12% latency improvement on our internal p99 tests versus October. these numbers are early but promising.
[02:05] Elena: awesome, can you say a little about cost uplift or tradeoffs?
[02:20] Priya: sure, autoscaling reduces idle cost but adds a bit of tail latency during cold starts; ops has tuned warm pools to mitigate, net unit cost is down ~6% for the average customer in our benchmark. caveat: workloads with extreme burst patterns still see higher percentiles.
[03:10] Tariq (VP Eng): engineering notes: we shipped the kernel selection pipeline and a new quantization profile that helps on A100 and H100 stacks. small note, there was an outage on Nov 28 tied to the cache invalidation path in prefix KV cache — we'll talk about that in reliability.
[04:00] Ben (Head Ops): summarizing Nov 28 incident quickly: a bad rollout triggered inconsistent cache state across nodes, causing elevated error rates and retries; impact window ~12 minutes, mitigations included immediate rollback and forced cache clear. customers were notified within 20 minutes.
[04:50] Elena: thanks Ben, appreciate the quick response. lessons learned?
[05:05] Ben: stronger canary rules, automated consistency checks, and a manual kill-switch for cache invalidation rollouts. Tariq s team is codifying this in runbook.
[05:40] Marcus: technical detail — the inconsistency was due to version skew in the KV layer when a mixed fleet had two kernel sets; we reworked the deployment orchestration to ensure version pins across the cluster during rollouts.
[06:15] Audience: (unintelligible) question about private on-prem timing...
[06:30] Priya: Private GA plan: we re baselined to mid-Q1 2027 for broad GA after some security hardening and KMS integration work. pilot customers are live in early access and feedback has been strong around the VPC control plane. note: we still have to finish HSM/KMS edge cases for some regulated customers.
[07:10] Elena: timeline implications for sales? Sara?
[07:25] Sara (Head Sales): we re messaging mid Q1 and offering pilot slots, pipeline looks healthy, but a few EAA deals are waiting on SOC2 scope expansion and on-prem options, so expect some asks.
[08:00] Priya: we re also enabling better rollout controls in the console: canary percent, region pinning, pricing previews per model variant. demo next quarter.
[08:50] Marcus: on performance — we re seeing good gains from continuous batching and some kernel optimizations, but we re tracking a small regression on a 65B model when run with very long seq lengths; working with model onboarding to reduce mem pressure.
[09:35] Elena: high level metrics — revenue and usage: we closed the quarter up 28% vs previous quarter in usage dollars, hosted API grew but dedicated commitments were the majority of new ARR. churn stayed low at ~2.1% monthly, NPS ticked up slightly.
[10:15] Audience (someone): applause emoji in chat.
[10:25] Jules (Head People): hiring update: we hired 18 folks in Q4, onboarding throughput improving, but we re prioritizing SRE, infra perf, and sales engineers for Q1. hiring freeze? no, just more targeted.
[11:00] Elena: a reminder on compensation and end of year reviews — managers will post calibration notes next week, open doc in HR.
[11:28] Priya: product roadmap bullets: Q1 2027 priorities: 1) Private GA (mid-Q1), 2) Dedicated autoscale enhancements (Q1), 3) Redwood Optimize v2 with smarter batching suggestions (Q1/Q2), 4) improved console observability for per-route cost breakdown (Q1).
[12:20] Marcus: engineering bets for Q1: focus on reliability (canaries, rollout safety), quantization improvements for Llama-family and mix-precision on H100, and runtime memory compaction to support longer KV caches.
[13:05] Ben: Ops focus — better runbooks, incident postmortems published within 72 hours, expanded on-call rotations and a pager duty change to reduce fatigue.
[13:45] Sara: go-to-market: we re aligning marketing and sales on three use-cases: low-latency customer-facing chat, high-throughput embedding pipelines, and private/regulatory deployments. expect new case studies in Jan.
[14:20] Audience question (typed): pricing changes?
[14:35] Elena: no across-the-board price increases planned; we ll continue to optimize unit cost and pass some benefits to customers where possible. we re also exploring packaging changes for dedicated commits to improve predictability.
[15:05] Priya: product note on pricing tooling: console will show estimated token cost per model variant and a suggested quantization profile that balances perf vs cost.
[15:45] Tariq: infra note — we re reducing some cross-region replication default retention to save storage costs; customers with longer retention needs can opt in.
[16:10] Audience: question about SOC2 and compliance timeline.
[16:25] Elena: SOC2 Type 2 report is on track for Q2 2027 for the expanded scope; we re engaging auditors and tightening audit logs and SSO flows.
[16:55] Priya: security investments: SSO/SAML improvements, RBAC in console, KMS/HSM integrations for Private customers, and longer audit retention for enterprise.
[17:30] Audience: (someone mispronounces) KV cache as "kay vee cash" in chat, people laugh.
[17:50] Marcus: small demo note — we re adding better tracing hooks so customers can attribute per-token cost and latency to code paths; this will help benchmarking for enterprise cases.
[18:30] Elena: financial tidbits — Q4 burn is slightly below plan thanks to ops improvements and slower infra spend; runway extended by incremental revenue and lower cloud egress for some partnerships.
[19:10] Jules: culture and benefits — holiday schedule reminder, volunteer day next month, and mental health days for everyone.
[19:45] Sara: customer highlights — three larger deals closed this month, one expansion with fintech customer moving to dedicated, another SSO-first enterprise moving to private pilot.
[20:20] Audience / Q&A: we ll open mic for questions, please use the raise hand or chat.
[20:40] Q1 (Engineer in Seattle): can you share more about the rollback policy that triggered the outage? was it automated?
[21:05] Ben: it was a partially automated rollout that allowed a new invalidation path; the rollback was manual after alerts; we re changing this to a stricter canary gate and auto-rollback on consistency mismatches.
[21:45] Q2 (Sales AE): curious re Private pilot onboarding friction — what s the biggest blocker?
[22:05] Priya: two things: KMS/HSM integration and customer network setup; we re adding more onboarding automation and a network checklist.
[22:40] Q3 (SRE): will the new quantization profiles be exposed per-model?
[22:55] Marcus: yes per-model and per-variant in the console; also an API flag to opt into experimental profiles.
[23:25] Q4 (Product Manager): any changes to roadmap priorities if we see more pilot demand?
[23:45] Elena: we re flexible; we ll prioritize customers that show high enterprise fit and have potential for anchored commitments; product will evaluate and re-sync with GTM.
[24:10] Audience: (background chatter)
[24:30] Priya: quick shoutout to the infra team for the kernel selection pipeline rollout — big win.
[24:45] Marcus: shoutout to sales ops for closing the fintech expansion test case.
[25:05] Elena: thank you all for hard work this year, few housekeeping items: holiday schedule doc, last day for end-of-year reviews, and a reminder to fill the internal survey.
[25:30] Audience: applause emoji, chat hearts.
[25:45] Ben: reminder — we re publishing the Nov 28 postmortem and a remediation timeline by next week.
[26:05] Jules: HR note — office reopenings in Jan will be flexible; we re monitoring commute patterns.
[26:30] Sara: we ll run a customer-facing webinar on Dedicated in mid-Jan, product to help with slides.
[26:50] Priya: I will share roadmap deck and schedule demo slots by next Friday.
[27:10] Elena: OK closing — thank you, happy holidays, we ll follow up with the deck and action items.
[27:30] Meeting end (recording stopped).

Notes on transcription quality: medium, some speaker overlaps and occasional mis-typed product names.
